title: Lettermail Size and Weight Limits in Canada
description: Standard letters go up to 245×156×5 mm and 50 g; non-standard and oversize to 380×270×20 mm and 500 g. Minimums and what raises the price.
keywords: canada post envelope sizes and rates
answer: Standard Canadian Lettermail is up to 245 × 156 × 5 millimetres and 50 grams. Non-standard and oversize Lettermail goes up to 380 × 270 × 20 millimetres and 500 grams. Larger or heavier items stop being Lettermail and must be sent as parcels, at parcel prices.

blocks.p: In inches, a standard item is 9.6 × 6.1 × 0.2, and the largest Lettermail item is 14.9 × 10.6 × 0.8.
A square envelope between 140 × 140 mm and 156 × 156 mm is priced as standard. Other items outside the standard dimensions are priced as non-standard or oversize.

ol: Measure the sealed envelope itself, not the paper inside: length, height, then thickness at the thickest point.
Compare it with the standard limits. If any one dimension is over, it is non-standard or oversize.
Weigh it. Weight sets the price band; size decides which price table applies.
Seal it. An unsealed item is not priced as a standard letter.

blocks.p: A standard letter will usually hit a weight line long before it hits the 5 mm thickness limit, because paper is thin. A card with a bump, a key or a padded insert is the usual way to exceed the thickness.

Canada Post says that a letter larger than the maximum dimensions must use its parcel services. Parcel services have their own prices and delivery standards. What each band costs is in [letter rates by weight](/blog/canada-post-letter-rates-by-weight).
